settings.name_in_paper: Recommendation game: incentive-compatible exploration with agents uncertain about arrival time (adversarial bandits)
unmapped: Recommendations are made to a sequence of myopic agents who may deviate; the guarantee is the approximation error epsilon of an incentive-compatible Bayes-Nash equilibrium, not regret
Each agent holds a private reward belief P^i (distribution over mean-reward sequences) and a temporal belief D^i over her arrival time; the mechanism does not know these beliefs
Agents' beliefs satisfy explorability (each action is Delta-better under D-marginalized means with prob >= alpha) and slowly-moving means (||mu_{t+1}-mu_t||_inf <= rho)
settings.definition_quote: A new agent arrives and receives a recommendation $I_t \in A$ from the algorithm ... The environment selects a reward vector $u_t \in [0,1]^K$ independently of $I_t$ ... The agent chooses an action $a_t \in A$, possibly deviating from the recommendation. The algorithm observes the played action $a_t$ and the corresponding reward $u_t(a_t)$.

bound.regime: each eta term counts only when positive, else +infinity

symbols.R_swap: expected D^i-weighted swap regret guaranteed by the algorithm
symbols.Psi_max: max dispersion of the temporal belief D^i
symbols.rho: slow-moving drift bound of believed mean rewards

conditions: Agents' beliefs satisfy Assumption 4.1 (explorability with (alpha, Delta)) and Assumption 4.2 (slowly moving, rho)
algorithm guarantees expected D^i-weighted swap regret R_swap for all agents i

source.label: thm:BIC-swap
source.quote: If an algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ played over $T$ rounds guarantees expected $\mathcal{D}^i$-weighted swap regret $R_{\emph{Swap}}^{(\mathcal{D}^i)}(T)$ for all $i \in [T]$, then $\mathcal{A}$ implements an incentive-compatible Bayes $\epsilon(T)$-Nash equilibrium with error term for agent $i$: \epsilon_i(T) = \min\{\eta_{\Psi}(T),\, \eta_{\Phi}(T), 1\}.

results.notes: Bound is on the IC-BNE approximation error epsilon_i, not regret; reduction for any algorithm with weighted swap regret guarantees.

bound.regime: each eta term counts only when positive, else +infinity

symbols.R_ext: expected D^i-weighted external regret guaranteed by the algorithm

conditions: Assumptions 4.1 and 4.2 hold for all agents' beliefs with (alpha, Delta, rho)
algorithm guarantees expected D^i-weighted external regret R_ext for all i

source.label: thm:BIC-ext
source.quote: If an algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ played over $T$ rounds guarantees expected $\mathcal{D}^i$-weighted external regret $R^{(\mathcal{D}^i)}(T)$ for all $i \in [T]$, then $\mathcal{A}$ implements an incentive-compatible Bayes $\epsilon(T)$-Nash equilibrium with error term for agent $i$: \epsilon_i(T) = \min\{\eta_{\Psi}(T),\, \eta_{\Phi}(T), 1\}.

bound.regime: o(1) when L = omega_tilde(sqrt(T)) and rho = o(1/L)

symbols.L: length of the agent's uniform temporal-belief window

conditions: each agent's temporal belief is uniform over a contiguous interval of length L
Assumptions 4.1 and 4.2 hold with (alpha, Delta, rho)

source.label: thm:uniform-first
source.quote: If agent $i$'s temporal belief is uniform over a subsequence of length $L$, then Exp4.S with parameter $T$ implements an incentive-compatible Bayes $\epsilon(T)$-Nash equilibrium where the error term for agent $i$ is: ... Specifically, when $L = \tilde{\omega}(\sqrt{T})$, and $\rho = o(1/L)$, we have vanishing error $\epsilon_i(T) = o(1)$.

results.notes: O() appears only on the regret term inside the expression in the paper; recorded with notation O.

results.notes: IC-BNE error; K dependence hidden in O_tilde.
